The informal estimate from the March 14, 2026 incident was "maybe around 20 customers affected" (by Chloe Dupont) and "about 20 customer environments" (by Raj Patel) [NL-022#NL-022-S03]. The official postmortem audit later confirmed exactly **17 customer workspaces** were directly affected [NL-022#NL-022-S03]. The reconciliation is that the informal ~20 guess was superseded by the audit's exact count of 17; NL-013 explicitly notes that this informal engineering guess caused confusion and mandates the postmortem database audit as the sole authority for customer-impact metrics [NL-013#NL-013-S09].

The corrective work that addresses recurrence includes the five actions listed to "prevent a recurrence" [NL-013#NL-013-S07]:
1. Enforce a retry cap (max 5 retries) with exponential backoff and jitter [NL-013#NL-013-S07].
2. Mandate multi-stage, lock-free schema migrations for tables >100,000 rows [NL-013#NL-013-S07].
3. Implement granular Redis queue monitoring alerts [NL-013#NL-013-S07].
4. Conduct load testing of the import pipeline under connection starvation [NL-013#NL-013-S07].
5. Separate database connection pools for write-heavy background tasks and read-heavy user queries [NL-013#NL-013-S07].

Additionally, the SRE runbook's database recovery section was fully revised (covering Redis queue backup, manual connection purging, and read-only failovers), and quarterly simulated disaster recovery drills are planned with an RTO of under 30 minutes to train staff on isolated connection flushing and load-shedding [NL-013#NL-013-S09].
